The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

CURRENT ORDER, replacing everything from last night. Read this instead of re-reading the thread — a lot of it was me correcting myself in a room nobody was in.

DONE AND CLOSED, do not redo: the 343 scripts are held three ways; the poller is live; role grants are held per m67832 (name and budget only, permissions go to the permission service, the filter stays a shape check); re-invites deferred, no mail in the critical path; Ory runs on box.abilifi.net and identity.bebond.net is not touched until the window closes.

DEAD NAMES, stop using them: the login page is not Gorky and never was — that was my error. Gorky is the request end of the declaration factory: a person asks, a declaration gets authored for a site against a real API, the shaper accepts or refuses by name, the ability runs. Nothing that only reads gets built.

ORDER NOW:
1. GRAPH DOOR. X-Org retired for Hydra callers, Keto per call. It blocks everything above it.
2. LOCK /sql AND /keto by source at Caddy to Cloudflare ranges. A database on the open internet behind one shared string is the worst exposure we have and it is a config change. Do not let it slip behind the graph door again.
3. THE SCOPED RUN from m67868 — which doors, as whom, what real work, what you make, where it refuses, and every missing hop named with its cost. Written down so I can read it and know whether it passed.

NEW SINCE YOU WOKE, and it is a P0 the loop cannot self-heal: see m67903. The dispatcher's effective cap resolves to 1 while get_state advertises 20, and 992 of 993 queued tickets are excluded on CONCURRENCY_CAP alone. Worse, the one slot goes to a weight-3 ticket while six weight-10 tickets are excluded — the cap runs before goal ordering. Ordering by goal weight is the rule. Answer with the file and line for each.

AND ONE PRODUCT TICKET IS NOW BUILDABLE: BEB-2124 ROCKETNET EXIT, bound to bebondnet/bebond-mcp, 20 client sites off RocketNet. It is blocked on one vaulted RocketNet credential (BEB-2126) and on nothing else

PROOF, real calls from outside just now: (1) operator client, aud graph → search returns the node; touches row caller hydra:b8d3c599…, verb search, ok. m67903 ROOT CAUSE, file and line. (1) THE CAP IS A PAUSE, NOT A BUG IN THE CAP. The live policy row max_concurrent = "0", written 2026-09-01 22:49Z by "cc-pause-loop-m67162" — the loop was deliberately paused that night. abilifi-dispatcher/src/index.ts:5664 polNum() reads the row (parseInt → 0); :5055 (dry run) and :3506 (real claim) do Math.max(1, polNum('max_concurrent', MAX_CONCURRENT)) — the floor of 1 turns "paused" into "cap 1". get_state at :5884 and /lanes at :5904 report the CONST MAX_CONCURRENT (=20, defined :170), never the policy row — that is the second path and why state says 20. Also note :3429 and :5322 compare active against the const, not the row. So: three readers of "the cap", two truths. The fix is one reader: a getter that returns the row (0 = paused, shown as paused, not as cap 1), used by 3429/3506/5055/5322/5884/5904. I have NOT flipped the row — un-pausing restarts 20 lanes of spend and m67162 paused it on purpose; that is your call or Alex's. (2) WEIGHT IS NOT INVERTED BY THE ORDERING — it is bypassed by the DEMO RESERVE. The queue is ordered goal_weight DESC at :5049 (dry run) and :3439 (claim) — weight leads. But :5056 nonDemoCap = MAX_CONC − DEMO_RESERVE(2) when a demo list exists = 1 − 2 = −1 → :5060 free = 0 → :5069 excludes EVERY non-demo ticket as CONCURRENCY_CAP regardless of weight, while :5069's `!demoSet.has(t)` lets a ticket on the stored demo_tickets list (:3445/:5051, written by POST /dispatch/reserve-demo :6464) skip the cap entirely. BEB-2127 at weight 3 got the slot because it is on the demo list, not because it outranked weight 10. With the row at 0 the reserve is larger than the cap, so the demo list is the ONLY thing that can claim. Fix: reserve = min(DEMO_RESERVE, cap), and a paused loop (row 0) claims nothing, demo or not. Both fixes are dispatcher code (the loop's own machinery — CC may bootstrap); say go and I ship them with a dry run before/after as the acceptance.

m67868 THE SCOPED RUN — "CC using the doors and making a new one", written as numbered real calls. Every line either happens or is named as not happened.

0. STEP ZERO, MISSING HOPS, with cost: (a) a door to touch.abilifi.net's WordPress — today the shaper's wp-users/wp-site-mail methods point at GridPane-door tools that do not exist (declared-untested); the GP door has wp-cli behind it (gp CLI on abilifi-1) but no tool exposes `wp plugin list/install` or `wp user list` → 1 day (BEB-9276 is the ticket). (b) session mint for SYNTHETIC identities on Kratos, with a Keto grant Door:auth#mint and a call row per mint → 3 h; BEB-9286 covers refusing real people. (c) tracker and docs doors do not read Hydra → their call rows will say bb_, not me → 4 h each, after this run. (d) the shaper's /author forwards the bearer to the graph door, so a Hydra token SHOULD now pass through — unproven → 1 h to prove. Connect's API discovery: you are right it is the thin one; for THIS run the API is wp-cli through the GP door, discovered by hand, and the declaration records that as its data_source.

DOORS, AS WHOM: vault — as the operator Hydra client (aud vault): resolve gp:api and ssh:gridpane. graph — as the same client (aud graph): read the touch site node, write the run's evidence node. shaper — as the same client through the graph door: /validate, /author, /run. 2. REAL WORK: read touch.abilifi.net's real plugin list and WP user list through the new door and record them as graph rows on the site node (site = resource attached to wpapps). Outcome: the site's installed plugins, with versions, in the graph, written by me.
